title: Counted loops
goal: Write a terminating loop for a known number of items and explain how its total changes.

prerequisites.text: Handle the result of a validated read.

terms.title: Counter
terms.definition: A variable that identifies the current repetition.

terms.title: Accumulator
terms.definition: A value holding the result for the part processed so far.

terms.title: Iteration
terms.definition: One execution of the loop body. Its condition is checked before the body.

sections.title: Why it matters
paragraphs: A warehouse knows its batch size before reading the weights. Start the counter at zero and process exactly that many records. Do not consume the first weight of the next batch.
A for loop initialises once, then checks the condition, runs the body and advances the loop variable. With i = 0 and i < n, the body visits indices 0 through n − 1.
Before each repetition, total equals the sum of values already processed. Adding the current weight preserves that property for the next step.

sections.title: Seats in four rows
paragraphs: Row number row contains 3 * row seats. Trace the loop in the listing and write the running totals.
The example starts at row 1 and ends at row 4. In the practice task, count how many records were processed starting from zero.
steps: Initialise total once before the loop.
Compare row with 4 before the body.
Print the total when the condition becomes false.

sections.title: One iteration too many or too few
paragraphs: With zero-based counting, i <= n consumes an extra record. At n = 0 the body unexpectedly runs once.
Initialising total inside the body destroys the old sum. If a read fails before the required count, do not report the partial total as the full batch.
A for header has two semicolons. Omitting the first leaves the compiler unable to separate initialisation from the condition.

sections.title: Check the ends of the batch-size range
paragraphs: Try n = 0 and n = 1. Ten weights of 200 sum to at most 2000, within the minimum C17 range of int.
After an error following a valid read, the accumulator holds a partial total. The batch contract calls for invalid because the complete batch was not read.

reading.author: ISO/IEC JTC1/SC22/WG14
reading.title: ISO/IEC 9899:2018 — Programming languages — C
reading.purpose: Review the for execution sequence and the guaranteed minimum int range.

selfcheck.prompt: How many times does the body of for (int i = 0; i < 0; ++i) execute?
feedback: The condition is checked before the body.
The first test is already false.

selfcheck.prompt: Why must n = 3 with only two weight lines print invalid even if the partial sum is reasonable?
selfcheck.feedback: The third attempted read returns READ_END. The contract requires every weight. A partial sum does not give the weight of the entire batch.

practice.title: Weigh a batch of boxes
practice.task: The first line gives a batch size from 0 to 10. Read exactly that many following lines with weights from 0 to 200. Print weight and the sum. Print only invalid if any required record is missing or invalid. Ignore input after a complete batch.
practice.hint: After a successful read, add weight to total inside the loop. Initialise total before the loop.
criteria: The sum is 0 before reading weights.
Each valid weight contributes exactly once.
A missing weight gives only invalid. A size of 0 gives weight 0.

steps.action: Add the accumulator update and test size 0.
steps.why: An empty loop leaves the initial value intact.

steps.action: Remove the last line from a batch of three.
steps.why: End of input before the limit leaves the batch incomplete.
steps.expected: The program prints invalid without a partial weight.

exercises.title: Locate an extra read
exercises.task: Predict the result for size 1, weight 4 and an extra line 999. Explain how to detect an accidental i <= boxes.
criteria: The extra repetition reads 999 and unexpectedly prints invalid.
